bullets.title: 30yr Treasury hits 5.33%, highest since 2007; tech and duration assets pressured
bullets.body: Global bond yields are rising in concert across US, Japan, Germany, and France, with the US 30-year reaching 5.33% and Japan's 10-year at a 30-year high of 2.95%. Multiple desks cite AI-related corporate bond issuance (August hitting a third straight monthly record), US fiscal deterioration ($1.17T YTD deficit, debt-to-GDP on path to 120% by 2036), and BOJ/JPY dynamics as drivers. NDX futures fell 1.2% and semis led losses, with JPM calling yields the primary headwind to tech multiples; the 10-year yield at 4.74% is at the top of Hedgeye's risk range.

bullets.title: Hormuz shutdown intensifies: COSCO/CMES halt tanker traffic; diesel crack hits record $102
bullets.body: Chinese shipping giants COSCO and CMES suspended oil tanker transit through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb after a UKMTO-reported projectile strike on a vessel in the Strait. WTI settled at $84.50 (+2.55%) and Brent at $90.87 (+2.65%). Diesel crack spreads hit a record $102/bbl, and Wolfe Research estimates a 'no war, no peace' equilibrium is the base case, with Polymarket pricing 60% odds of an Oman-Iran deal by month-end. Trump rejected extending the MOU and floated declaring Hormuz a US territory.

bullets.title: BofA Fund Manager Survey shows near-record bullish positioning; AI bubble flagged as top tail risk
bullets.body: BofA's latest Global Fund Manager Survey reflects third-most-bullish sentiment since 2022, with 56% net OW global equities, cash at 3.5%, and 56% predicting 'no landing.' Semis are the most crowded trade (down 30pp to 52% net OW). AI bubble is the most-cited tail risk. JPM notes NDX long positions cut to historically low levels (-1.6z) by asset managers, with software positioning near 4th-percentile lows—suggesting short covering rather than fresh longs driving recent moves.

bullets.title: Anthropic ARR reaches $65B in July, up from $47B in May; AI demand debate around $80B+ speculation
bullets.body: Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate hit $65B by end of July (7x YoY), surpassing OpenAI's. Jefferies called the print 'lighter than recent speculation of $80B+,' noting some coding/agentic workload share was lost to OpenAI, Deepseek, and Kimi K3. OpenAI ARR separately surpassed $40B with 20% MoM growth in July and cut GPT-5.6 prices 50% on OpenRouter. Anthropic is targeting an IPO within ~2 months at a reported $190-200B 2028 revenue-based valuation.

bullets.title: NVIDIA backs $105B of OpenAI Ohio data center; Spectrum-X CPO in mass production
bullets.body: NVIDIA agreed to backstop up to $105B of OpenAI's 20-year Ohio data center lease (revised from an initial $250B figure), with first 800MW of 8GW capacity targeted for 2028 and potential $600B in chip revenue through 2030. Separately, NVIDIA's Spectrum-X CPO (co-packaged optics) switches entered mass production with TSMC, Foxconn, and ASE as partners. UBS estimates NVDA will generate ~$1B/day in FCF; NVDA is the most under-owned mega-cap vs S&P 500 at -2.53%.

bullets.title: Semis under heavy pressure in pre-market: MRVL -5.7%, COHR -5.9%, LITE -6.1%, MU -4.2%
bullets.body: The broad semiconductor complex is being hit by a combination of rising yields, Anthropic ARR disappointment vs. $80B+ rumors, and general risk-off. Pre-market: LITE -6.1%, COHR -5.9%, MRVL -5.7%, STX/WDC -5.6%, AAOI -4.2%, MU -4.2%, AMD -3.2%. Semiconductor ETF (SMH) 1M implied vol fell 5.4 pts to 36.4 (41st pct) while realized vol is at 45.8 (80th pct), and semi outflows of -$3.9B were tracked by JPM.

bullets.title: HBM demand set to nearly double by 2028; NVDA captures 35-40% of supply
bullets.body: HBM demand is projected to grow from 6.5-7 exabytes in 2027 to 12.5EB in 2028. Meritz Securities forecasts Broadcom could surpass NVDA as the largest HBM consumer by 2028 (35-40bn Gb vs NVDA's 30bn Gb), with Google at 20bn and AMD at 10bn. NVDA has already secured 35-40% of 2027 global HBM supply. MU management notes supply/demand in 2027 tighter than 2026, fulfilling less than 50% of data center customer volume requests with HBM ASPs expected +79% YoY.

bullets.title: S&P 500 Q2 EPS on track for >$90 (+33% YoY); UBS targets SPX 8100 YE
bullets.body: UBS reports 77% of S&P 500 firms beat Q2 EPS, with Tech OCF jumping $383B YoY (+37%). SPX Q2 EPS tracking above $90, 7.4% above expectations. 2027 EPS estimates revised up 3.7% to $406. UBS targets SPX 8100 at year-end based on $410 2027 EPS at 19.8x P/E, noting upside risks if Iran and rates are contained. Equity positioning in software is near historical lows (4th-percentile), while regional banks' L/S ratio approaches multi-year highs (74th-percentile).

bullets.title: US fiscal deterioration intensifies: debt interest at 3.3% of GDP, record pace of borrowing
bullets.body: US interest payments hit 3.3% of GDP, an all-time high, while YTD deficit stands at $1.17T (+15% YoY) with national debt approaching $40T. Investment-grade corporate bond issuance hit a third straight August monthly record, partly AI-capex driven; BofA estimates this pushed 10-year yields up ~0.3pp YTD. Yield curve steepened to new cycle highs: 10yr-2yr spread at +55bps vs +23bps in late June. The 1990s analogy fails because M2 is accelerating, not slowing, and defense/interest costs lack a 'peace dividend' offset.

bullets.title: US-Iran standoff entrenched; Hedgeye and Wolfe see higher-for-longer oil, no near-term resolution
bullets.body: Wolfe Research's base case is a 'no war, no peace' equilibrium persisting for 'some time,' noting US magazine depth concerns and Iran's real but non-regime-threatening economic pain. Trump rejected extending the MOU and signaled no urgency on talks, while Kushner described conversations as 'more robust than ever.' Oil up ~50% YTD; WTI near $85 with crack spreads at records. Hedgeye flags Quad 3 stagflation regime with oil and commodities bullish and consumer discretionary (XLY) as a short.

bullets.title: Home Depot Q2 beats: comps +1.7% vs +0.9% consensus; reiterated FY guidance
bullets.body: HD reported Q2 adjusted EPS of $4.92 vs $4.73 consensus, with comps of +1.7% (US +1.3% vs consensus +0.8%). 13 of 16 merchandise departments saw increases, the highest since 2022, driven by small-project demand and Pro outperformance. Gross margin expanded ~30bps to 33.7% aided by ~$500-540M in IEEPA tariff refunds. FY guidance reiterated. Citi and UBS both maintain Buy, with UBS at $430 PT; the result is read as broadly positive for consumer spending despite 'frozen housing market' conditions.

bullets.title: META faces landmark $200B child addiction trial; 29 states suing across nation's largest consumer protection case
bullets.body: A federal bellwether trial opened Monday with 29 states seeking up to $200B in damages and platform changes including removal of infinite scroll and recommendation algorithms, and restrictions on youth users. META's theoretical maximum penalty exposure could reach $1.4T per the company's own disclosures, though appeals are expected. META was down 1.1% pre-market. The trial is expected to be a prolonged overhang.

bullets.title: Global bond yields rising in concert across G7; Japan 30yr hits record 4.13%, Germany 10yr at 3.22%
bullets.body: Japan's 30-year JGB yield rose to 4.13% (record high); 10-year hit 2.95% (30-year high); 5-year hit a record 2.18%. Germany's 10-year yield reached 3.22%, highest since May 2011, and France-Germany spreads widened to 86bps (widest since Oct 2025). Multiple sources characterize the synchronous global move as a bearish regime shift for equities, with one analyst noting a 100bp move today carries the impact equivalent of 300bp in the 1990s due to market duration extension.

bullets.title: Financials on 11-week winning streak (record); energy +39% YTD; semis/software underperform
bullets.body: JPM notes financials have rallied for 11 consecutive weeks, the longest streak on record, with L/S ratios approaching multi-year highs. Energy is +39% YTD vs SPX +13.1%. Energy was the only sector in the green Monday, with positive breadth while all other sectors fell. Software positioning is at historical lows (4th-percentile), and the S&P 500 equal-weight underperformed the cap-weighted index by nearly 2x on Monday.

bullets.title: Chase consumer spending data shows acceleration: MTD August +5.6% YoY vs July +4.4%
bullets.body: JPMorgan's internal Chase card data shows August MTD spending through Aug 7 up 5.6% YoY vs July's 4.4%, with Gen Z and Millennials at +8.8% YoY and discretionary up +6.1%. The data is broad-based across income quintiles and suggests underlying consumer demand remains intact, offering a partial counterweight to macro yield concerns.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO imminent; OpenAI Ohio deal structures suggest AI financing becoming next bottleneck
bullets.body: Anthropic is targeting an IPO within ~2 months with a valuation case built around $190-200B in projected 2028 revenues. The NVDA-backed OpenAI Ohio deal highlights AI infrastructure financing as an emerging constraint beyond technology: NVDA is providing residual-value support to unlock broader insurance and institutional capital. WSJ reported $3T in AI off-balance-sheet liabilities growing $1.2T per quarter. SoftBank plans $6.3B retail bond issuance separately.

bullets.title: UK labour market cools: payrolls -13K in June, private wage growth slows to 2.8%
bullets.body: UK June payrolled employees fell 13K vs 0K expected; employment growth (3M/3M) came in at 84K vs 138K consensus. ILO unemployment held at 4.9% (slightly above BoE's 4.8% projection). Private sector regular pay decelerated from 2.9% to 2.8% YoY, below the BoE's ~3.25% target-consistent level. The data was 'a bit softer overall' per Barclays, with GBP briefly under pressure, though alternative pay trackers (Indeed, DMP) remain in the 3.5-4.0% range.

bullets.title: NVDA Aug 26 earnings and Jackson Hole Aug 27-29 flagged as pivotal near-term catalysts
bullets.body: JPM and Hedgeye both flag NVDA's earnings on Aug 26 and Jackson Hole (Aug 27-29) as the next major events that could shift market narrative. Hedgeye's NVDA data-center revenue model claims 97% R-squared; Blackwell GPU rental prices are showing 'tremendous strength' while Hopper pricing was flat in Q2. UBS estimates NVDA generates ~$1B/day in FCF, with consensus revenue ranging $630-681B.

bullets.title: AAPL services business hurt by App Store regulatory changes; China removing Windows from state users
bullets.body: Apple acknowledged that App Store regulatory changes are hurting its $100B+ services business. Separately, Citi notes Apple is being urged by the Trump administration not to source memory from Chinese suppliers. China is also removing Windows from state users ahead of schedule, per MSFT. These items compound regulatory headwinds for the two largest market-cap names in tech heading into a rate-sensitive tape.

bullets.title: Nasdaq to launch 9pm-4am ET overnight trading session on December 6, 2026
bullets.body: Nasdaq announced it will introduce a new overnight trading session from 9pm to 4am ET starting December 6, 2026, engaging regulators to enable nearly 23-hour continuous weekday trading. The session will have fewer order types and reduced regulatory protections vs. regular hours. The move is part of a broader shift toward near-continuous markets.
